clauses: The checks are applied in this order and the first check that fails decides the claim: 1) required document; 2) waiting periods; 3) exclusions; 4) notification deadline.

No benefit is payable for an item if the incident happened fewer days after the policy start date than the waiting period of its category (start date = day 0; see the schedule). An item inside its waiting period is dropped from the claim; the other items continue.
A claim must be notified within 14 days after the incident date (the incident date is day 0); later notification is not accepted.
Every claim must include the inventory list. If it is missing, the claim is held and nothing is paid until it is supplied.
If any exclusion below applies to the facts of the claim, nothing is payable for the whole claim.
A deductible of A$400.00 applies once per claim: each item is first limited to its category sublimit, and the deductible is then subtracted from the sum of the limited items.
The insurer pays 80% of the amount remaining after the deductible and sublimits; the business owner bears the rest.
Total payments in one policy year may not exceed A$10000.00. Amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains, and a payout is cut to what remains.

Release of payments: amounts up to A$500.00 are paid automatically, above A$500.00 up to A$1500.00 need supervisor sign-off, above A$1500.00 need the claims committee. Claims where nothing is payable now are level 0.
All amounts are rounded half up to the smallest currency unit after each step.
The insurer processes personal data only to assess claims and to prevent fraud.
This policy is governed by the law of the country in which the policyholder lives.

event_rules: Events are applied in ascending order of ts; events with the same ts keep their order in the list.

A status event sets the ticket's status to its value if the ticket is not "merged" or "closed"; for a "closed" ticket it is rejected. Moving to "open" is only accepted from "resolved" (a reopen); every other transition is accepted.
An assign event sets the ticket's assignee to its value, unless the ticket is "closed" or "merged" (rejected).

A merge event (ticket = source, value = target ticket) sets the source to "merged" and its assignee is unchanged; the target ticket takes the smaller (more urgent) priority number of the two. A merge is rejected if the source or the target is "closed" or "merged", or if source and target are the same.

A void event cancels the effect of the event whose id is in its target field, as if that event had never happened (all remaining events are applied again without it). A void can itself not be voided; a void whose target id is not in the log is ignored.
A rejected event has no effect at all and does not change the entity.

Ereignisregeln: Ereignisse werden in aufsteigender Reihenfolge von ts angewendet; Ereignisse mit gleichem ts behalten ihre Reihenfolge in der Liste.

Ein status-Ereignis setzt den Status des Tickets auf seinen Wert, wenn das Ticket nicht „zusammengeführt“ oder „geschlossen“ ist; bei einem Ticket mit „geschlossen“ wird es abgelehnt. Der Wechsel zu „offen“ wird nur aus „gelöst“ akzeptiert (Wiedereröffnung); jeder andere Übergang wird akzeptiert.
Ein assign-Ereignis setzt den Bearbeiter des Tickets auf seinen Wert, es sei denn, das Ticket ist „geschlossen“ oder „zusammengeführt“ (abgelehnt).

Ein merge-Ereignis (ticket = Quelle, value = Ziel-Ticket) setzt die Quelle auf „zusammengeführt“, ihr Bearbeiter bleibt unverändert; das Ziel-Ticket übernimmt die kleinere (dringendere) Prioritätszahl der beiden. Ein merge wird abgelehnt, wenn Quelle oder Ziel „geschlossen“ oder „zusammengeführt“ ist oder Quelle und Ziel identisch sind.

Ein void-Ereignis hebt die Wirkung des Ereignisses auf, dessen id im Feld target steht, als wäre es nie geschehen (alle übrigen Ereignisse werden ohne es erneut angewendet). Ein void kann selbst nicht aufgehoben werden; ein void, dessen Ziel-id nicht im Protokoll steht, wird ignoriert.
Ein abgelehntes Ereignis hat keinerlei Wirkung und verändert das Objekt nicht.

правила_событий: События применяются в порядке возрастания время; события с одинаковым время сохраняют порядок в списке.

Событие статус устанавливает статус тикета в своё значение, если тикет не «объединена» и не «закрыта»; для тикета «закрыта» оно отклоняется. Переход в «открыта» принимается только из «решена» (повторное открытие); любой другой переход принимается.
Событие назначение назначает исполнителя тикета на своё значение, если только тикет не «закрыта» или «объединена» (отклоняется).

Событие слияние (тикет = источник, значение = целевой тикет) переводит источник в «объединена», исполнитель источника не меняется; целевой тикет получает меньший (более срочный) номер приоритета из двух. Merge отклоняется, если источник или цель «закрыта» или «объединена», либо источник и цель совпадают.

Событие аннулирование отменяет действие события, чей номер указан в поле цель, как если бы оно никогда не происходило (остальные события применяются заново без него). Сам аннулирование отменить нельзя; аннулирование, чей целевой номер отсутствует в журнале, игнорируется.
Отклонённое событие не имеет никакого эффекта и не изменяет объект.

event_rules: Events are applied in ascending order of ts; events with the same ts keep their order in the list.

A status event sets the ticket's status to its value if the ticket is not "merged" or "closed"; for a "closed" ticket it is rejected. Moving to "open" is only accepted from "resolved" (a reopen); every other transition is accepted.
An assign event sets the ticket's assignee to its value, unless the ticket is "closed" or "merged" (rejected).

A merge event (ticket = source, value = target ticket) sets the source to "merged" and its assignee is unchanged; the target ticket takes the smaller (more urgent) priority number of the two. A merge is rejected if the source or the target is "closed" or "merged", or if source and target are the same.

A void event cancels the effect of the event whose id is in its target field, as if that event had never happened (all remaining events are applied again without it). A void can itself not be voided; a void whose target id is not in the log is ignored.
A rejected event has no effect at all and does not change the entity.

rules: Process the events in order of their timestamp (the list is in arrival order). Every ticket starts as "open". Allowed moves: "assign" takes "open" to "assigned"; "start" takes "assigned" to "in_progress"; "resolve" takes "in_progress" to "resolved"; "close" takes "resolved" to "closed"; "reopen" takes "resolved" or "closed" back to "in_progress". An event that does not fit the ticket's current status is ignored and leaves no trace.

The second "reopen" that is actually applied to a ticket sends it to "escalated" instead of "in_progress"; "escalated" is final and every later event on that ticket is ignored. "undo" returns a ticket to the status it had before its most recent applied move (repeated "undo" events step back further; an "undo" with nothing to undo is ignored; undoing a reopen also takes it out of the reopen count).

Regeln: Verarbeiten Sie die Ereignisse nach ihrem Zeitstempel (die Liste steht in Eingangsreihenfolge). Jedes Ticket beginnt als „offen“. Erlaubte Übergänge: „zuweisen“ führt von „offen“ zu „zugewiesen“; „starten“ von „zugewiesen“ zu „in_Arbeit“; „lösen“ von „in_Arbeit“ zu „gelöst“; „schließen“ von „gelöst“ zu „geschlossen“; „wiedereröffnen“ von „gelöst“ oder „geschlossen“ zurück zu „in_Arbeit“. Ein Ereignis, das nicht zum aktuellen Status des Tickets passt, wird ignoriert und hinterlässt keine Spur.

Die zweite tatsächlich angewendete „wiedereröffnen“ eines Tickets führt nicht zu „in_Arbeit“, sondern zu „eskaliert“; „eskaliert“ ist endgültig, und jedes spätere Ereignis dieses Tickets wird ignoriert. „rückgängig“ setzt ein Ticket auf den Status vor seinem letzten angewendeten Übergang zurück (wiederholtes „rückgängig“ geht weiter zurück; ein „rückgängig“ ohne etwas Rückgängig-zu-Machendes wird ignoriert; das Rückgängigmachen einer Wiedereröffnung nimmt sie auch aus der Zählung).

Una pequeña cadena de panaderías tenía que abrir tres sucursales nuevas en un solo mes, y la propietaria, la Sra. Adeyemi, necesitaba asignar a sus tres gerentes con más experiencia, Tobias, Ursula y Wanjiru, uno a cada sucursal. La sucursal Harbour era un establecimiento con mucho volumen de trabajo en una terminal de ferris muy concurrida, donde el ajetreo de primera hora de la mañana empezaba a las cinco y la cola podía llegar hasta fuera del local; necesitaba a alguien capaz de soportar un ritmo incesante y organizar a una plantilla numerosa. La sucursal Old Town era una panadería tranquila, tipo cafetería, en una calle peatonal, donde los clientes habituales esperaban charlar y recibir una recomendación personalizada, y donde se había admirado al gerente anterior por recordar los nombres. La sucursal University era un mostrador en un edificio universitario que abría hasta tarde, cerraba a medianoche y dependía de estudiantes con trabajos a tiempo parcial que a menudo cancelaban sus turnos en el último momento.

Tobias había dirigido anteriormente el establecimiento más concurrido del centro de la ciudad, donde había reducido los tiempos de espera a la mitad. No le gustaba la conversación trivial y pensaba que los clientes habituales podían «ir a otro sitio». Era madrugador, prefería el horario diurno y en una ocasión se había negado a trabajar un turno de cierre porque eso «le arruinaría la semana». Ursula era extrovertida, recordaba los nombres de los hijos de los clientes y sus encargos de cumpleaños; había dirigido una cafetería de barrio durante diez años. Odiaba tener que gestionar cuadrantes numerosos y cambiantes, pero no le importaban los horarios tardíos. Wanjiru mantenía la calma en medio del caos: había pasado años organizando los turnos del personal temporal de una cadena hotelera, gestionaba las cancelaciones repentinas sin quejarse y dormía a horas intempestivas por elección propia. No le entusiasmaba el turno temprano, pero no tenía nada en contra de las tardes largas. Tenía poca paciencia con los clientes parlanchines.

La Sra. Adeyemi también señaló que Tobias y Wanjiru se llevaban bien en el trabajo y compartían piso, mientras que Ursula había pedido no trabajar con Tobias porque una vez habían discutido por una receta. Las tres sucursales celebrarían reuniones conjuntas semanales, y la Sra. Adeyemi quería que reinara la paz en ellas.

The parties wish to discuss the possibility of evaluating a data-sharing pilot for fleet maintenance (the “Purpose”) and in that context the Disclosing Party is prepared to disclose certain information to the Receiving Party.

1. Definitions. “Confidential Information” means only written or electronic materials that the Disclosing Party has clearly marked “Confidential” at the time of disclosure. Oral and visual disclosures are not Confidential Information.

2. Scope of disclosure. Only the Disclosing Party will disclose Confidential Information under this Agreement; the other party acts solely as the Receiving Party.

3. Language. This Agreement is made in English. Any translation is for convenience only.

4. Remedies. The sole and exclusive remedy of the Disclosing Party for any breach of this Agreement shall be monetary damages; neither party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief.

5. Reverse engineering. The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer, disassemble or decompile any prototype, software or other tangible object that embodies Confidential Information.

6. Audit of security. On request, a party shall describe in general terms the security measures it applies to its own information systems.

7. Unauthorised disclosure. The Receiving Party has no obligation to inform the Disclosing Party of any unauthorised use or disclosure that it discovers, but it shall take reasonable steps to stop it.

8. Non-solicitation. Nothing in this Agreement restricts either party from soliciting or hiring any employee of the other party.

9. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for a delay in performing its obligations to the extent that the delay is caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that it gives prompt notice to the other party.

10. Term and termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving the other party thirty (30) days' written notice.

11. Permitted use. The Receiving Party shall use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and for no other purpose.

12. No obligation to proceed. Nothing in this Agreement obliges either party to enter into any further agreement or to disclose any particular information.

13. Rights in the information. The Disclosing Party grants the Receiving Party a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the Confidential Information for the Purpose during the term of this Agreement.

14. Anti-corruption. Each party shall comply with applicable anti-bribery laws in connection with the discussions and shall not offer any improper payment to any person.

15. Marking of materials. The Disclosing Party may, but is not required to, add a legend to documents it provides; the absence of a legend does not by itself affect any right of either party.

16. Duration of obligations. The obligations of the Receiving Party under this Agreement shall continue for a period of 7 years after the termination or expiry of this Agreement.

17. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement, (b) was lawfully known to the Receiving Party before disclosure, (c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of the Confidential Information, or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction.

18. Disclosure to personnel. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information only to its Representatives who need to know it for the Purpose. “Representatives” means the directors, officers, employees, professional advisers, affiliates and subcontractors of the Receiving Party.

19. Compelled disclosure. If the Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or court order to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the Disclosing Party prompt prior written notice where legally permitted and shall disclose only the portion that is legally required.

state.policy:
Travel and Expense Policy. This policy governs reimbursement of business-trip expenses for employees. Amounts are in euros.
1. Definitions. A "business trip" is a trip with at least one overnight stay away from the employee's home city that has been approved in advance. A "travel day" is any calendar day from the day of departure to the day of return, both included. "Grade" is the employee's grade from 1 to 4 as shown on the claim. City class A, B or C is assigned to the destination in Annex 1.
2. Hotel. The hotel is reimbursed per night up to the cap for the city class and grade (euros per night): class A: 160 (grades 1-2) / 180 (grades 3-4); class B: 115 (grades 1-2) / 140 (grades 3-4); class C: 95 (grades 1-2) / 120 (grades 3-4). Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed; the cap applies to every night.
3. Meals. Meals are reimbursed as a flat allowance of 40 euros per travel day. On the first and the last travel day the allowance is 50 % of that amount. For each meal that was provided free of charge (for example at a conference), the allowance of that travel day is reduced by 20 % of the full daily amount for breakfast and 30 % for lunch or dinner; the allowance of a day never falls below zero. No receipts are needed for the allowance.
4. Flights. Flights are reimbursed at the economy fare. Business class is reimbursed in full only if the flight lasts more than 5 hours and the employee is grade 4 or higher; otherwise the reimbursement is limited to the economy fare that the claim states for the same flight.
5. Local transport. Public transport and taxis at the destination are reimbursed up to 25 euros per travel day in total. Items of more than 25 euros need an original receipt. Items of up to 25 euros without a receipt are reimbursed only if those items together do not exceed 75 euros; otherwise none of them is reimbursed.
6. Excluded items. Alcoholic drinks, minibar, personal entertainment and leisure, spa and fitness, parking fines and any other fines are never reimbursed, even if they appear on a hotel invoice.
7. Private car. If the employee uses a private car, mileage is reimbursed at 0.30 euros per kilometre. This clause does not apply to taxis or rented cars.
8. Late claims. A claim must be submitted within 45 days after the day of return. If it is submitted later but within 75 days, the total reimbursable amount is reduced by 10 %. After 75 days the claim is rejected.
9. Approval. The approver is determined by the total reimbursable amount after all deductions: up to and including 500 euros the line manager approves; above that and up to and including 2000 euros the department head approves; above 2000 euros the finance director approves. A rejected claim needs no approval.
10. Records. Claims and receipts are kept for ten years. Personal data on receipts is processed under the company data protection notice.
Additional provisions (these do not change the numbered clauses above):
- Advance payments. Employees may request an advance of up to 70 % of the expected hotel and travel costs, at the earliest ten days before departure. Advances are settled against the claim and do not change the rules for reimbursement.
- Trips abroad. For trips to destinations outside the home country a separate foreign-travel annex applies, with country-specific meal allowances between 55 and 95 euros per day. The annex is not part of this policy and is issued by the finance department.
- Training trips. Travel to external training events is booked through the learning platform. The registration fee is paid centrally and does not appear on the claim.
- Spouses and guests. Costs for accompanying persons are never reimbursed, including their share of a shared room or meal.
Annex 1. City classes: A = capital and financial centres; B = other cities above 250,000 inhabitants; C = all other places.

Regra 2: quando o modo passa a night: definir garage_heat=26, porch_plug=off, living_light=on@20

semântica: Os eventos são processados estritamente na ordem listada. Depois de um evento, as regras correspondentes disparam em ordem crescente de número e cada ação é aplicada imediatamente.
Uma regra com condição só dispara se a condição for verdadeira nesse momento; uma regra marcada como «única» só dispara na primeira vez em que o gatilho e a condição coincidem.

Um comando direto do usuário define o dispositivo e o coloca em retenção manual. Ações de automação sobre um dispositivo retido são ignoradas até o próximo evento de «modo», que libera todas as retenções antes de suas regras dispararem. Comandos não disparam regras por si só.
Uma fechadura não pode ser colocada em «locked» enquanto o sensor da porta indicar «open»: a ação é ignorada (a fechadura mantém o valor e nada muda). Destrancar é sempre possível.
As temperaturas do termostato (dispositivos heat) são limitadas à faixa 17-25: um valor maior ou menor é gravado como o limite mais próximo.

Quando um dispositivo realmente muda de valor (causada por um comando do usuário ou por uma regra; não há mudança se já tinha esse valor), as regras com gatilho «o dispositivo passa a valor» entram na fila e disparam depois das regras próprias do evento atual, na ordem das mudanças.
Códigos de valor: on@N = luz acesa com N % de brilho, off, on/off para tomadas, locked/unlocked, open/closed para persianas, um número = temperatura do termostato em °C.

Rule 2: when motion is detected in living and the current mode is not home: set nursery_plug=off, garage_plug=on

semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.
A lock cannot be set to locked while its door sensor reads open: the action is ignored (the lock keeps its value, and no change happens). Unlocking is always possible.
Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 17-25: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.

Automatisierungsregeln: Regel 1: wenn der Modus home wird: setze office_heat=28, garden_light=on@70, living_blind=closed
Regel 2: wenn Bewegung in living erkannt wird und der aktuelle Modus nicht away ist: setze office_plug=off, bedroom_blind=closed
Regel 3: wenn lock_living den Wert locked annimmt: setze living_plug=off, garden_light=on@100
Regel 4 (einmalig): wenn door_studio den Wert open annimmt: setze garden_light=on@30
Regel 5: wenn door_studio den Wert closed annimmt: setze living_blind=open
Regel 6: wenn die Uhr 22:00 erreicht und der aktuelle Modus vacation ist: setze bedroom_blind=open, living_blind=open, garden_heat=21
Regel 7: wenn Bewegung in bedroom erkannt wird und der aktuelle Modus movie ist: setze office_plug=off
Semantik: Die Ereignisse werden strikt in der angegebenen Reihenfolge verarbeitet. Nach einem Ereignis feuern die passenden Regeln in aufsteigender Regelnummer, und jede Aktion wird sofort ausgeführt.
Eine Regel mit Bedingung feuert nur, wenn die Bedingung in diesem Moment gilt; eine mit „einmalig“ markierte Regel feuert nur beim ersten Mal, wenn Auslöser und Bedingung passen.

Ein direkter Benutzerbefehl setzt das Gerät und versetzt es in manuelle Sperre. Automatik-Aktionen auf einem gesperrten Gerät werden übersprungen, bis das nächste „Modus“-Ereignis kommt; dieses hebt alle Sperren auf, bevor seine Regeln feuern. Befehle lösen von sich aus keine Regeln aus.

Ein Schloss kann nicht auf „locked“ gesetzt werden, solange der Türsensor „open“ meldet: die Aktion wird ignoriert (das Schloss behält seinen Wert, es ändert sich nichts). Entriegeln ist immer möglich.
Thermostat-Sollwerte (Heiz-Geräte) sind auf den Bereich 17-24 begrenzt: ein größerer oder kleinerer Wert wird als nächstliegende Grenze gespeichert.

Ändert ein Gerät tatsächlich seinen Wert (durch einen Nutzerbefehl oder eine Regel verursacht; keine Änderung, wenn es den Wert schon hatte), werden Regeln mit dem Auslöser „Gerät wird Wert“ eingereiht und feuern nach den eigenen Regeln des aktuellen Ereignisses, in der Reihenfolge der Änderungen.

自动化规则: 规则 1: 当`cellar`检测到移动时 且当前模式为`eco`，设置 cellar_plug=`on`, bedroom_light=`off`
规则 2: 当模式变为`guest`时，设置 living_light=`on@100`, bedroom_heat=`16`
规则 3: 当lock_living变为`unlocked`时，设置 bedroom_heat=`15`, cellar_heat=`28`
规则 4: 当模式变为`night`时，设置 lock_bedroom=`locked`, cellar_heat=`20`, lock_living=`locked`
规则 5 （仅一次）: 当时钟到达`06:30`时 且当前模式为`home`，设置 hall_blind=`closed`, lock_bedroom=`unlocked`, bedroom_light=`on@100`
行为规则: 事件严格按列出的顺序处理。一个事件发生后，匹配的规则按规则编号从小到大触发，每个动作立即生效。
带条件的规则只有在当时条件成立时才触发；标记为“仅一次”的规则只在触发器和条件第一次匹配时触发。
用户的直接命令会设置设备，并使其进入手动保持。对处于保持状态的设备的自动化动作会被跳过，直到下一个“模式”事件；该事件在其规则触发之前解除所有保持。命令本身不会触发规则。
门传感器显示 open 时，门锁不能设为 locked：该动作被忽略（门锁保持原值，没有任何变化）。解锁始终可以。
恒温器设定值（heat 设备）限制在 17-25 的范围内：过大或过小的值会按最接近的上下限保存。
当设备确实改变了值（无论由用户命令还是规则引起；如果本来就是该值则不算变化），以“设备变为某值”为触发器的规则会进入队列，在当前事件自己的规则之后，按变化发生的顺序触发。
数值代码：on@N = 灯亮度 N % 开启，off，插座为 on/off，门锁为 locked/unlocked，百叶窗为 open/closed，数字 = 恒温器设定温度（°C）。

questions.instructions: 所有事件之后，bedroom_heat是否被设为`28`？

自動化ルール: ルール 1: lock_garageが`unlocked`になったとき かつ現在のモードが`guest`のとき，設定 garage_heat=`20`
ルール 2: 時計が`07:00`になったとき，設定 hall_blind=`closed`, kitchen_plug=`on`
ルール 3 （一度だけ）: door_garageが`closed`になったとき，設定 studio_blind=`open`, studio_plug=`off`
ルール 4: モードが`night`になったとき，設定 bedroom_light=`on@50`, lock_kitchen=`locked`, garage_heat=`16`
ルール 5: モードが`guest`になったとき，設定 lock_kitchen=`locked`, garage_heat=`24`, kitchen_blind=`closed`
ルール 6: `studio`で動きを検知したとき かつ現在のモードが`away`でないとき，設定 studio_plug=`off`, bedroom_blind=`open`
ルール 7: モードが`movie`になったとき，設定 kitchen_blind=`open`, hall_heat=`16`, hall_blind=`open`
イベント（順番どおり）: 1. ユーザーコマンド：lock_garageを`unlocked`に設定
8. ユーザーコマンド：bedroom_plugを`off`に設定
9. ユーザーコマンド：studio_blindを`closed`に設定
動作仕様: イベントは記載された順に厳密に処理されます。イベントの後、一致するルールがルール番号の昇順で発火し、各アクションは直ちに適用されます。
条件付きのルールは、その時点で条件が成り立つ場合にのみ発火します。「一度だけ」と記されたルールは、トリガーと条件が最初に一致したときだけ発火します。
ユーザーの直接コマンドはデバイスを設定し、手動ホールドにします。ホールド中のデバイスへの自動化アクションは、次の「モード」イベントまでスキップされます。モードイベントは、そのルールが発火する前にすべてのホールドを解除します。コマンド自体はルールを発火させません。
ドアセンサーが open を示している間は、錠を locked にできません。そのアクションは無視されます（錠は元の値のままで、変化は起きません）。解錠は常に可能です。
サーモスタットの設定温度（heat デバイス）は 18-26 の範囲に制限され、範囲外の値は最も近い上限または下限として保存されます。
デバイスが実際に値を変えたとき（ユーザーコマンドまたはルールによるもの。すでにその値なら変化なし）、「デバイスが値になったとき」というトリガーのルールがキューに入り、現在のイベント自身のルールの後に、変化が起きた順に発火します。
値コード：on@N = 明るさ N % で点灯、off、プラグは on/off、錠は locked/unlocked、ブラインドは open/closed、数値 = サーモスタットの設定温度（°C）。

policy: Rules are numbered. A call is executed only if no rule forbids it and every requirement that applies to it is met. A "forbidden" rule always beats any requirement or permission. Roles in ascending order: viewer < agent < analyst < manager < admin.

policy.title: Personal Data Handling Policy
rating_rules: Impact class: A = no records; B = up to 100 records; C = 101 to 5,000 records; D = more than 5,000 records, or any incident where notification of the data protection authority is required. The class is set by the highest criterion met. (Impact is measured as stated in the investigation report.)
Base level: Class A = 0, B = 1, C = 2, D = 3.
Add 1 level if the act was deliberate (the employee knew the rule and chose to break it).

Add 1 level once if there is at least one substantiated violation of this same policy within the 12 months (365 days) before the date of this incident; violations that were not substantiated or were withdrawn do not count.
Subtract 1 level if the employee reported the matter themselves within 24 hours of discovery and the act was not deliberate.
A first-ever violation (no substantiated violation on record at all) cannot be rated above Level 2 unless the impact class is D.
Adjustments are applied together; the final level is limited to 0-3.

policy.title: Arbeitssicherheitsregeln
rating_rules: Wirkungsklasse: A = keine Verletzung; B = Verletzung mit bis zu 3 Ausfalltagen; C = 4 bis 30 Ausfalltage; D = mehr als 30 Ausfalltage, oder jeder Vorfall, bei dem eine gesetzliche Unfallanzeige erforderlich ist. Maßgeblich ist das höchste erfüllte Kriterium. (Die Wirkung wird so gemessen, wie es der Untersuchungsbericht angibt.)
Punkte: Klasse A = 0, B = 1, C = 3, D = 5.
Addiere 2 Punkte bei Vorsatz (die Person kannte die Regel und verstieß bewusst dagegen).
Addiere 1 Punkt je bestätigtem Verstoß gegen dieselbe Richtlinie in den 12 Monaten (365 Tagen) vor dem Vorfall, höchstens 2 Punkte; nicht bestätigte oder zurückgezogene Verstöße zählen nicht.

Ziehe 1 Punkt ab, wenn die Person den Vorfall innerhalb von 24 Stunden nach Entdeckung selbst gemeldet hat und die Tat nicht vorsätzlich war. Ziehe 1 Punkt ab, wenn der Bericht volle Kooperation festhält. Addiere 1 Punkt, wenn die Person eine leitende Rolle hat (Teamleitung oder höher).
Die Punktsumme kann nicht unter 0 fallen. Stufen: 0-1 Punkte = Stufe 0; 2-3 Punkte = Stufe 1; 4-5 Punkte = Stufe 2; 6 oder mehr = Stufe 3.

policy.title: Standard kontroli wydatków i płatności
rating_rules: Klasa wpływu: A = brak niezatwierdzonych wydatków; B = do 1 000 EUR; C = od 1 001 do 25 000 EUR; D = ponad 25 000 EUR albo każdy incydent, w którym płatność trafiła do odbiorcy objętego sankcjami lub zablokowanego. Klasę wyznacza najwyższe spełnione kryterium. (Wpływ mierzy się tak, jak podano w raporcie z dochodzenia.)
Punkty: klasa A = 0, B = 1, C = 3, D = 5.
Dodaj 2 punkty, jeśli czyn był umyślny (osoba znała zasadę i świadomie ją złamała).
Dodaj 1 punkt za każde potwierdzone naruszenie tej samej polityki w ciągu 12 miesięcy (365 dni) przed incydentem, maksymalnie 2 punkty; naruszenia niepotwierdzone lub wycofane nie liczą się.

Odejmij 1 punkt, jeśli osoba sama zgłosiła sprawę w ciągu 24 godzin od wykrycia, a czyn nie był umyślny. Odejmij 1 punkt, jeśli dochodzenie odnotowało pełną współpracę. Dodaj 1 punkt, jeśli osoba zajmuje wyższe stanowisko (kierownik zespołu lub wyżej).
Suma nie może spaść poniżej 0. Poziomy: 0-1 punkt = poziom 0; 2-3 punkty = poziom 1; 4-5 punktów = poziom 2; 6 lub więcej = poziom 3.

Hạng được xác định theo tiêu chí cao nhất được đáp ứng. (Tác động được đo như nêu trong báo cáo điều tra.)

Cộng 1 mức nếu hành vi là cố ý (người đó biết quy định và vẫn cố tình vi phạm).
Cộng 1 mức một lần nếu trong 12 tháng (365 ngày) trước sự cố có ít nhất một vi phạm đã được xác nhận đối với cùng chính sách này; vi phạm không được xác nhận hoặc đã rút lại thì không tính.
Trừ 1 mức nếu người đó tự báo cáo trong vòng 24 giờ sau khi bị phát hiện và hành vi không cố ý.

state.problem: I have two tables, customers and blocked_ids. This query is supposed to show customers who are not blocked: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM blocked_ids). It returns zero rows although I know thousands qualify, and the blocked list is only a handful of rows. I added one row recently where the customer id was left empty. What's going on?
documents: D1. Conditional Aggregation: To compute several counts in one pass, use aggregate functions over CASE expressions, for example SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). The FILTER clause (FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')) does the same in dialects that support it. It avoids multiple scans or self-joins.

D2. Filtering on Window Results: Window functions are evaluated after WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING, so their results cannot be referenced in those clauses. To keep only the first row per group, compute ROW_NUMBER() in a subquery or common table expression and filter on it in the outer query. Some dialects offer QUALIFY to filter directly.

D3. Comparisons With Unknown Values: In SQL, comparing anything with NULL using = or <> yields UNKNOWN, not true or false. A WHERE clause keeps only rows where the condition is true, so rows with unknown results disappear. Use IS NULL, IS NOT NULL or IS DISTINCT FROM to test for missing values explicitly. This also means that a row with a NULL does not satisfy either col = 1 or col <> 1.

D4. Aggregates and Missing Values: Aggregate functions such as SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX ignore NULL inputs. COUNT(column) counts non-null values while COUNT(*) counts rows. AVG over a column with NULLs divides by the number of non-null values, not the number of rows. If the group has only NULLs, SUM and AVG return NULL rather than 0; wrap with COALESCE when a zero is wanted.

D5. Range Requests: A client may ask for part of a resource with a Range header, and the server answers 206 Partial Content with a Content-Range header. Download managers and video players use this to resume or seek. Servers advertise support with Accept-Ranges: bytes.

D6. Taints and Tolerations: A node taint such as dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule repels pods that do not carry a matching toleration. Tolerating a taint only permits scheduling there; it does not attract the pod. Combine a toleration with a node selector or affinity rule if the pod should land on the tainted nodes.

D7. Rounding in Division: In many databases dividing two integer columns performs integer division, so 7 / 2 returns 3. Cast one operand to a decimal or multiply by 1.0 first. The rounding mode of ROUND on exact halves also differs: some systems round half away from zero while others round half to even.

D8. Sorting With Missing Values: Where NULLs appear in an ORDER BY depends on the system: some treat NULL as larger than any value, so it sorts last in ascending order, others as smaller. NULLS FIRST and NULLS LAST make the placement explicit. The same choice affects how LAG, FIRST_VALUE and top-N queries behave.

D9. Rounding Modes and Half Cases: IEEE 754 default rounding is round-half-to-even, so 0.5 rounds to 0 and 1.5 and 2.5 both round to 2 in functions that follow it. Python's round uses it, while many spreadsheets round halves away from zero. Because many decimals are not exact in binary, a value that looks like a half may actually lie slightly above or below it.

D10. Priority and Preemption: Pods with a higher PriorityClass can cause the scheduler to evict lower priority pods to make room when the cluster is full. Evicted pods are rescheduled elsewhere if possible. Preemption never evicts pods of equal or higher priority.

D11. no-cache Versus no-store: Cache-Control: no-cache does not forbid storing: it requires the cache to revalidate with the origin before every reuse. no-store forbids storing the response at all, which is appropriate for sensitive data. Confusing the two is a common cause of either stale or needlessly uncached pages.

D12. NOT IN With Subqueries: x NOT IN (subquery) is evaluated as a chain of <> comparisons joined by AND. If the subquery returns even one NULL, the result for every x is UNKNOWN or false, so the query returns no rows. NOT EXISTS with a correlated condition, or filtering the subquery with WHERE col IS NOT NULL, avoids the surprise.

D13. Numbering Rows: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK: ROW_NUMBER assigns unique consecutive numbers even for ties, in an order that is arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is made unique. RANK gives tied rows the same number and then skips ahead. DENSE_RANK gives tied rows the same number and does not skip. Choose according to whether gaps and ties matter.

D14. Join Types and Unmatched Rows: An INNER JOIN keeps only pairs that satisfy the condition. A LEFT JOIN additionally keeps every left row, filling right columns with NULL when no match exists. Placing a condition on a right-table column in the WHERE clause turns the LEFT JOIN back into an inner join because NULL rows are filtered out; put the condition in the ON clause instead to keep unmatched left rows.

D15. Node Affinity and Selectors: A nodeSelector or requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity restricts a pod to nodes whose labels match. If no node has the required labels, the pod stays Pending with an event stating that no nodes matched the node affinity or selector. Preferred affinities only influence scoring.

D16. Binary Fractions Cannot Express Most Decimals: Floating-point numbers store values as a binary fraction times a power of two. Decimal values such as 0.1 or 0.7 have infinite binary expansions and are stored as the nearest representable double, so 0.1 + 0.2 evaluates to 0.30000000000000004. Comparing floats for equality is therefore fragile; compare with a tolerance or use a decimal type for money.

D17. Integer Overflow and Wraparound: Fixed-width integers wrap around when a result exceeds their range: in 32-bit two's complement, 2147483647 + 1 becomes -2147483648. Some languages trap overflow, others silently wrap. Intermediate products, such as in (a * b) / c, can overflow even when the final result fits. Use wider types or reorder the operations.

D18. Parsing and Printing Round Trips: A double printed with 17 significant digits can be read back to exactly the same value; printing with fewer digits may not round-trip. Shortest round-trip algorithms emit the minimal digits that parse back identically. Locale settings can change decimal separators and break parsing.

D19. Deduplicating With DISTINCT ON and GROUP BY: SELECT DISTINCT removes rows that are identical in all selected columns. To keep one full row per key, PostgreSQL offers DISTINCT ON (key) with an ORDER BY that picks which row survives; in other systems use ROW_NUMBER partitioned by the key. GROUP BY with non-aggregated extra columns is rejected by standard SQL.

D20. Immutable Fingerprinted Assets: Files whose names contain a content hash, such as app.3f9c1a.js, never change under that name, so they can be served with max-age=31536000 and the immutable directive. Browsers then skip revalidation even on reload. The HTML that references them must not be cached for long, or users keep requesting old file names.

D21. Default Frame for Running Totals: A window with ORDER BY and no frame clause uses RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. With RANGE, rows that tie on the ordering key are peers and are all included together, so a running SUM jumps by the whole group of tied rows at once. Specifying ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW counts physical rows one by one.

D22. Modulo and Division of Negative Numbers: Languages differ in the sign of the remainder: in C and Java -7 % 3 is -1, in Python it is 2 because the result takes the sign of the divisor. Integer division rounds toward zero in C and Java but toward negative infinity in Python. Wrapping indexes with a negative offset depends on this convention.

D23. stale-while-revalidate: The directive stale-while-revalidate=60 lets a cache serve a stale response for up to 60 seconds while it fetches a fresh copy in the background. Users get fast responses, and the next request sees the updated content. stale-if-error similarly permits serving stale content when the origin fails.

D24. Out-of-Memory Terminations: When a container exceeds its memory limit the kernel's OOM killer terminates it and Kubernetes records the reason OOMKilled with exit code 137. The pod restarts according to its restartPolicy, producing CrashLoopBackOff if it repeats. Raising the limit, reducing the process footprint or checking for leaks addresses the cause; the readiness probe is not involved.

D25. Looking at Neighbouring Rows: LAG(expr, n, default) returns the value from n rows before the current row in the window order, and LEAD looks forward. The first row of a partition has no predecessor, so LAG returns NULL there unless a default is supplied. They avoid a self-join when computing differences between consecutive rows.

D26. Liveness and Readiness Probes: A failing readiness probe removes the pod from Service endpoints but keeps it running. A failing liveness probe makes the kubelet restart the container. Slow starting applications should use a startupProbe so that liveness checks do not kill them before they are initialised.

documents: D1. Margin Collapsing: Vertical margins of adjacent block elements, or of a parent and its first or last child with no padding or border between them, combine into the larger of the two instead of adding. A child's top margin can therefore appear to push the parent down. Padding, a border, or establishing a new formatting context stops it.

D2. Interrupts and Cancellation: Thread.interrupt sets a flag and wakes blocking calls, which throw InterruptedException and clear the flag. Code that catches the exception and ignores it prevents cancellation. Restore the flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() or propagate the exception.

D3. Condition Waits and Spurious Wakeups: Object.wait can return without a notify, so the waiting condition must be rechecked in a loop: while (!ready) lock.wait(). Using an if statement risks proceeding while the condition is still false. Higher-level utilities such as CountDownLatch or BlockingQueue avoid this.

D4. Check-Then-Act Races: Code such as if (!map.containsKey(k)) map.put(k, v) is two operations; another thread can insert between them. Even with a thread-safe map each call is atomic but the sequence is not. Use putIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent, or synchronise the whole sequence.

D5. Unsafe Publication: Making an object reachable to other threads before its constructor finishes, for example by storing this in a static field inside the constructor, may expose partially initialised fields. Final fields get special guarantees; otherwise publish through a volatile reference, a lock or a concurrent collection.

D6. Lock Waiting Versus Slow Queries: A statement that is idle waiting for a row lock held by another open transaction looks slow, but its CPU and I/O are low. Looking at the lock wait list shows the blocker, often a transaction left open by an application that forgot to commit. Query plans cannot help here.

D7. Atomic Increment: The expression count++ on a shared int reads, adds and writes in separate steps, so concurrent increments can be lost. AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet performs the update atomically, and LongAdder scales better under heavy contention when only the final sum is needed.

D8. Memory Footprint of Threads: Each platform thread reserves a stack, commonly 512 KB to 1 MB, so creating tens of thousands exhausts memory or hits OS limits with an OutOfMemoryError about creating a native thread. Pools with bounded size, or virtual threads, serve many concurrent tasks.

D9. Non-Thread-Safe Library Classes: Classes such as SimpleDateFormat and ArrayList are not safe for concurrent use. Sharing one formatter between request threads yields garbled dates or exceptions that appear only under load. Use thread-confined instances, ThreadLocal, or immutable alternatives like DateTimeFormatter.

D10. ConcurrentModificationException: Structurally modifying a collection while iterating over it with an iterator or enhanced for loop throws this exception in the same thread, not only across threads. Use iterator.remove, collect removals and apply afterwards, or a concurrent collection that tolerates modification.

D11. Visibility Without Synchronisation: A thread may keep a variable in a register or cache, so a change made by another thread may never become visible. A loop that waits for a boolean field to turn true can spin forever. Declaring the field volatile or accessing it under a lock establishes a happens-before relationship that makes the write visible.

D12. Text Overflow and Ellipsis: text-overflow: ellipsis only works on a block that has overflow other than visible and white-space: nowrap, and on a defined width. In a flex or table layout the element may need min-width: 0 or a max-width for truncation to occur. Without all conditions, the text simply overflows.

D13. Parallel Streams and Shared State: A parallel stream runs a lambda on several threads from the common pool. Mutating a shared non-thread-safe collection inside forEach causes lost updates. Prefer collectors or reduction operations that combine thread-local partial results.

D14. Thread Pool Starvation: In a fixed-size pool, tasks that block waiting for other tasks submitted to the same pool can occupy all threads, leaving none to run the awaited tasks. The pool deadlocks without any lock being involved. Use separate pools for dependent work or non-blocking composition.

D15. Lock Ordering and Deadlock: If thread A holds lock 1 and waits for lock 2 while thread B holds lock 2 and waits for lock 1, neither proceeds. The standard fix is to acquire locks in a consistent global order. Thread dumps list the blocked threads and the locks they hold and wait for.

D16. Negative Caching: A lookup for a record that does not exist is a miss every time, and each one reaches the database. Caching the absence of a record for a short time prevents repeated queries for missing ids, which is especially useful when clients or attackers request random identifiers.
